preconditions.description: The graph has between 1 and 100,000 vertices and edges.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects distinct vertices within the valid range.
The input contains exactly m edges.
The number of edges is even (required for pairing).

preconditions.expression: all(edge not in edges[edges.index(edge)+1:] for edge in edges)
preconditions.description: The graph has no duplicate edges (simple graph).

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'No solution' or all(len(line.split()) == 3 for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Output is either 'No solution' or a list of valid paths of length 2.
If a solution exists, output contains exactly m/2 paths.

postconditions.expression: stdout != 'No solution' and all((x, y) in edges and (y, z) in edges for x, y, z in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()])
postconditions.description: Each path in the output is a valid length-2 path in the graph.

postconditions.expression: stdout != 'No solution' and len(set((x, y) for x, y, z in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()] + [(y, z) for x, y, z in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()]])) == m
postconditions.description: All edges are used exactly once across all paths.

postconditions.expression: stdout != 'No solution' or not any((x, y) in edges and (y, z) in edges and (x, y, z) not in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()] and (y, z) not in [(y, z) for x, y, z in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()]] for x, y, z in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()])
postconditions.description: No edge is reused in multiple paths (edge-distinct).
